entries.name: additive_noise

output.description: Noise standard deviation as a fraction of the reference field's fluctuation RMS, so 0.1 means noise a tenth the size of the field's own variation.

entries.summary: Adds independent Gaussian noise to every cell, with an amplitude set as a fraction of the reference field's fluctuation.

entries.name: band_attenuate

output.description: Fraction of the field's spectral energy above the cutoff that the filter removes, resolved per field to a cutoff wavenumber against a measured spectrum.

entries.summary: Weakens one chosen band of scales and leaves every larger and smaller scale untouched, by scaling down the Fourier modes between two fixed wavenumbers.

entries.name: bias

output.description: Offset as a fraction of the reference field's fluctuation RMS, so 0.5 shifts the field by half its own variation.

entries.summary: Adds a constant offset to every cell, shifting the whole field up or down without changing any spatial structure.

entries.name: box_blur

output.description: Kernel width in analysis-grid cells, rounded to an odd number, resolved per field from a severity given as a fraction of that field's characteristic scale.

entries.summary: Convolves the field with a square kernel of uniform weight, averaging every cell with its neighbours out to a fixed width.

entries.name: coarsen

output.description: Coarsening factor, a whole number of cells per block. Absolute rather than calibrated: a factor of four means four on every field.

entries.summary: Block-averages the field onto a coarser grid and expands it back, discarding everything below the block size.

entries.name: disk_blur

output.description: Kernel radius in analysis-grid cells, resolved per field from a severity given as a fraction of that field's characteristic scale.

entries.summary: Convolves the field with an isotropic disk kernel of a given radius, removing structure below that scale.

entries.name: epanechnikov_blur

output.description: Kernel radius in analysis-grid cells, resolved per field from a severity given as a fraction of that field's characteristic scale.

entries.summary: Convolves the field with an isotropic epanechnikov kernel of a given radius, removing structure below that scale.

entries.name: gain

output.description: Relative gain error: 0.1 means the fluctuation is scaled by 1.1, so every departure from the mean is a tenth too large.

entries.summary: Multiplies the field's fluctuation about its spatial mean by a constant factor, leaving the mean itself unchanged.

entries.name: gaussian_blur

output.description: Kernel standard deviation in analysis-grid cells, resolved per field from a severity given as a fraction of that field's characteristic scale.

entries.summary: Convolves the field with an isotropic Gaussian kernel, removing structure below the kernel width while leaving the large scales intact.

entries.name: gaussian_impostor

output.description: None. The severity is ignored entirely; there is one experiment, not a ladder.

entries.summary: Replaces the field with a Gaussian random field that has the same amplitude spectrum and the same low-order moments, but random phases.

entries.name: highpass_butterworth

output.description: Fraction of the field's spectral energy below the cutoff that the filter removes, resolved per field to a cutoff wavenumber against a measured spectrum.

entries.summary: Removes the large scales from the field by multiplying its Fourier transform by a smooth Butterworth high-pass transfer function.

entries.name: highpass_ideal

output.description: Fraction of the field's spectral energy below the cutoff that the filter removes, resolved per field to a cutoff wavenumber against a measured spectrum.

entries.summary: Removes the large scales from the field by multiplying its Fourier transform by a hard high-pass transfer function.

entries.name: identity

output.description: None. There is one level and it applies no change.

entries.summary: Returns the field unchanged. The level-zero reference against which every degradation is measured.

entries.name: lowpass_butterworth

output.description: Fraction of the field's spectral energy above the cutoff that the filter removes, resolved per field to a cutoff wavenumber against a measured spectrum.

entries.summary: Removes the small scales from the field by multiplying its Fourier transform by a smooth Butterworth low-pass transfer function.

entries.name: lowpass_ideal

output.description: Fraction of the field's spectral energy above the cutoff that the filter removes, resolved per field to a cutoff wavenumber against a measured spectrum.

entries.summary: Removes the small scales from the field by multiplying its Fourier transform by a hard low-pass transfer function.

entries.name: median_blur

output.description: Window width in analysis-grid cells, rounded to an odd number, resolved per field from a severity given as a fraction of that field's characteristic scale.

entries.summary: Replaces each cell with the median of a square neighbourhood, a nonlinear smoother that removes small features while leaving sharp edges in place.

entries.name: multiplicative_noise

output.description: Standard deviation of the multiplicative factor, relative: 0.1 means each cell is scaled by roughly one plus or minus a tenth.

entries.summary: Scales every cell by an independent random factor about one, so the perturbation is proportional to the local field value.

entries.name: random_large_translation

output.description: A draw index, not a severity. Each level is an independent random offset drawn from the same distribution; the levels are not ordered and carry no increasing damage.

entries.summary: Shifts the field by a large random displacement, producing a field that is statistically identical to the reference but positionally unrelated to it.

entries.name: subsample

output.description: Subsampling factor, a whole number of cells between retained samples. Absolute rather than calibrated.

entries.summary: Point-samples every Nth cell and expands the result back to the full grid, discarding the rest without averaging.

entries.name: translate

output.description: Displacement in whole analysis-grid cells, absolute rather than calibrated: one cell means one cell on every field.

entries.summary: Shifts the whole field by a whole number of cells along one axis, wrapping at the periodic boundary.

entries.name: translate_subpixel

output.description: Displacement in analysis-grid cells, continuous rather than rounded, absolute rather than calibrated.

entries.summary: Shifts the field by a fractional number of cells using a Fourier phase ramp, resolving displacements smaller than the grid spacing.

entries.name: enstrophy

output.description: Half the mean squared vorticity magnitude, summed over components, in the square of the vorticity units. Reported per variant; the drift from the reference is what is read.

entries.summary: Mean squared vorticity of a single field, a reference-free diagnostic of how much small-scale rotational activity a flow carries.

entries.name: kinetic_energy

output.description: Half the mean squared velocity magnitude, summed over components, in the square of the velocity units. Reported per variant; the drift from the reference is what is read.

entries.summary: Mean specific kinetic energy of a single velocity field, a reference-free diagnostic of how much energy the flow carries.

entries.name: mae

output.description: Mean over all channels and grid cells of the absolute field difference, in the field's own units.

entries.summary: Mean of the absolute difference between the candidate and reference fields, taken cell by cell on a common analysis grid.

entries.name: mse

output.description: Mean over all channels and grid cells of the squared field difference, in the square of the field's units.

entries.summary: Mean of the squared difference between the candidate and reference fields, taken cell by cell on a common analysis grid.

entries.name: nrmse

output.description: Dimensionless ratio of the root mean squared error to the reference field's fluctuation RMS. NaN where the reference is spatially uniform.

entries.summary: Root mean squared error divided by the root-mean-square fluctuation of the reference, giving a dimensionless error that can be read across fields.

entries.name: rmse

output.description: Square root of the mean over all channels and grid cells of the squared field difference, in the field's own units.

entries.summary: Square root of the mean squared difference between the candidate and reference fields, carrying the error back into the field's own units.
